inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months: The last documented fire drill was completed 9/18/2026.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))

occurrences.finding: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Not Over Concrete or Asphalt: The concrete was visible under the padding for the play equipment.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Not Over Concrete or Asphalt (26 TAC §746.4907(b))

occurrences.finding: Director's Absence -  Caregiver in Charge Has Access to All Records: Person in charge did not have access to the records.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director's Absence -  Caregiver in Charge Has Access to All Records (26 TAC §746.1013(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Health Statement: 1 out of 8 files did not have a health statement.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Health Statement (26 TAC §746.603(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Diaper Changing Equipment - No Play or Eating Surfaces Used: In the toddler room a child was being changed on a changing table that was on the floor near the other children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Diaper Changing Equipment - No Play or Eating Surfaces Used (26 TAC §746.3503(b))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Intervene to ensure each child's safety: A video was observed of two children fighting and the teacher did not intervene.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Intervene to ensure each child's safety (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(5))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: A teacher was observed sitting down while two kids were fighting on the playground and did not intervene.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: Based on information received during the DFPS investigation, it was determined that a caregiver took a child to their home unauthorized.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: No Smoking or Use of Tobacco Including E-Cigarettes or Vaporizers: Based on information received during the DFPS investigation there was enough information to determine that a staff was observed vaping while caring for kids on the playground.
occurrences.violation_type_title: No Smoking or Use of Tobacco Including E-Cigarettes or Vaporizers (26 TAC §746.3703(d))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Based on the information obtained during the DFPS investigation, a child was left unattended on the van when the caregiver made a stop at their home to use the restroom.  On another occasion, the caregiver also left children unattended on the van while the caregiver went in the school to get other children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Employees Supervised: Based on information received during the DFPS investigation the director allowed a caregiver to take a child in care away from the center to go and transport other children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Employees Supervised (26 TAC §746.1003(4))

occurrences.finding: Policies Comply with Rules: The operation did not ensure compliance with minimum standards related to the care, supervision, and protection of children. The permit holder did not adequately monitor staff practices or take timely action to correct know concerns resulting in children being placed at risk.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Policies Comply with Rules (26 TAC §746.201(1))

occurrences.finding: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited: During a DFPS investigation, it was determined that a caregiver physically abused a child in care.    During the investigation, it was determined that another caregiver physically neglected a child in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited (26 TAC §746.1201(4))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Orientation: During a DFPS investigation, it was determined that caregivers were not trained in discipline and guidance practices during orientation before having unsupervised access to children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Orientation (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(1)(A))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: During a DFPS investigation, it was determined that a caregiver left children in the classroom unsupervised when the caregiver went to the front office with another child.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance: During a DFPS investigation, it was determined that the director was aware staff were using inappropriate discipline practices with children and did not take appropriate action to address or stop the behavior or ensure compliance with minimum standards. The director also did not ensure staff received proper training related to discipline and guidance, and accepted training certificates not signed or verified by staff. Additionally, the director allowed children to be brought to the front office for the purpose of discipline and redirection, which is not an appropriate method of behavior guidance.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance (26 TAC §746.1003(1))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: During a DFPS investigation, it was determined that the operation did not report to Child Care Regulation that children were being inappropriately disciplined.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Corporal Punishment: During a DFPS investigation, there was evidence that a child was dragged from the classroom to the office as a form of punishment.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Corporal Punishment (26 TAC §746.2805(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: Evidence during a DFPS investigation determined that a caregiver did not exercise good judgment when the caregiver observed a child in care being physically abused and did not intervene.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Corporal Punishment: Based on information provided during the investigation inspection and interviews, there was enough information to support the allegation of prohibited punishment.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Corporal Punishment (26 TAC §746.2805(1))

occurrences.finding: Measurement of Use Zone for Slides - Six Feet High or Less: The use zones for the slide is less than six feet required.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Measurement of Use Zone for Slides - Six Feet High or Less (26 TAC §746.4805(b))

occurrences.finding: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Six Inches if Equipment 5 Ft or Less: The toddler playground equipment does not have the required amount of loose fill of 6 inches,
occurrences.violation_type_title: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Six Inches if Equipment 5 Ft or Less (26 TAC §746.4907(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Measurement of Use Zone for Slides - Six Feet High or Less: The use zones for the slide is less than six feet required.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Measurement of Use Zone for Slides - Six Feet High or Less (26 TAC §746.4805(b))

occurrences.finding: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Six Inches if Equipment 5 Ft or Less: The toddler playground equipment does not have the required amount of loose fill of 6 inches,
occurrences.violation_type_title: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Six Inches if Equipment 5 Ft or Less (26 TAC §746.4907(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Infant Care Area Furnishings and Equipment - Adult-sized Chair: In the infant room, there is no chair or rocking chair available in the area.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant Care Area Furnishings and Equipment - Adult-sized Chair (26 TAC §746.2405(1))

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Signed and Dated by Parent or Health-Care Professional: 2 out of 3 infants did not have their feeding instructions signed or dated by the parent.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Signed and Dated by Parent or Health-Care Professional (26 TAC §746.2421(a))

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Conducted by Fire Marshal: There was no current fire inspection available for viewing. The last fire marshal inspection was on 6/16/2022.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Conducted by Fire Marshal (26 TAC §746.5101(b))

occurrences.finding: Electronic Child Safety Alarm - Driver or designated employee conduct walk-through and visual check of vehicle: Walkthrough was not made throughout the vehicle, to ensure all children were drop off at school.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Electronic Child Safety Alarm - Driver or designated employee conduct walk-through and visual check of vehicle (26 TAC §746.5625(d)(2))

occurrences.finding: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk: Operation did not notify parents of child being left on the school bus.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk (26 TAC §746.307(b)(4))

occurrences.finding: Electronic Child Safety Alarm - Driver or designated employee verify all children accounted for: The bus driver did not ensure and verify all children were accounted for when dropping off the children at school and as result a child was left on the bus.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Electronic Child Safety Alarm - Driver or designated employee verify all children accounted for (26 TAC §746.5625(d)(1))

occurrences.finding: Electronic Child Safety Alarm - used at all times when transporting a child in care: The Safety Alarm on bus was turned off.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Electronic Child Safety Alarm - used at all times when transporting a child in care (26 TAC §746.5625(c))

occurrences.finding: Daily Menus - Record Comparable Substitutions: The food menu differed from the one posted at the operation.  Note: The director corrected it at inspection time.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Daily Menus - Record Comparable Substitutions (26 TAC §746.3313(1))

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months: The operation does not have a current annual fire inspection since 10/21/2020.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Health Statement: Ten children files were review. Nine of the ten children files do not have a statement of the child health from a medical professional.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Health Statement (26 TAC §746.603(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Annual Sanitation Inspection: The operation does not have a current annual sanitation inspection since 04/01/2020.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Sanitation Inspection (26 TAC §746.3401(a))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Free of other activities: One operational staff was observed texting a family member during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Free of other activities (26 TAC §746.1203(6))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: A child was seen running out of the classroom by himself to the director office.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children (26 TAC §746.1203(4))

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Related to Planned Activities: One child was observe playing a video game name Fornite on their hand-held device.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Screen Time Activities - Related to Planned Activities (26 TAC §746.2207(c)(1))

occurrences.finding: Nutrition and Food Service - Food not a reward: During the interview an operational staff stated that she use food as a bargain chip in order to get the children to compiling the center.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Nutrition and Food Service - Food not a reward (26 TAC §746.3301(h))

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training - 6 Hours of annual training required: The operational staff do not have the required annual training clock hours for guidance and discipline.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training - 6 Hours of annual training required (26 TAC §746.1309(b))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: A child can be seen leaving the classroom without proper adult supervision.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children (26 TAC §746.1203(4))

occurrences.finding: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: An operational staff can be seen mimicking a child behavior during an argument.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior (26 TAC §746.2803(4)(C))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: An operational staff is seen grabbing a child wrist during an argument.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))
